articles.title: Observers flag ‘fear, violence’ in first BARMM elections
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — The first-ever parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) marked a historic milestone for the peace process, but the exercise was…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — The first-ever parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) marked a historic milestone for the peace process, but the exercise was “severely undermined by systemic disenfranchisement, technical blunders, and a heavy military presence that sparked a climate of fear,” an election observer group reported.
In its preliminary report, the Commission on Elections (Comelec)-accredited Katungod Bangsamoro observer mission cited “glaring incidents of violence” during the Sept. 14 voting.

The consortium, which deployed monitors across Cotabato City, Maguindanao del Norte, and Maguindanao del Sur, rejected assertions that the elections were “generally peaceful,” warning that such a description trivializes the trauma, fear, and injuries that voters experienced.

“When a voter runs from a polling place because of gunfire, the right to vote has been effectively impaired,” Atty. Carlos Zarate, one of the observers of Katungod Bangsamoro, told the Inquirer Tuesday afternoon.
The group said it observed armed partisan confrontations, physical violence, and mob action in multiple areas, including Shariff Saydona Mustapha, Matanog, and Sultan Mastura.
In one incident at Nabundas Central Elementary School in Shariff Saydona Mustapha, voting was halted by 11:00 a.m. due to a nearby armed encounter, it noted.
“A prolonged exchange of gunfire, suggesting a running battle, could be heard roughly 250 meters outside the school,” Zarate texted this reporter late Monday afternoon.
Logistical and technical failures further disenfranchised voters, according to the group.

It observed that delayed election paraphernalia deterred early voting for senior citizens and persons with disabilities, while defective vote-counting machines (VCMs) were flagged in Upi, Datu Saudi Ampatuan, Datu Odin Sinsuat, and Shariff Aguak in the Maguindanao provinces.
The observers also documented instances of electoral board members allegedly feeding ballots directly into VCMs without the voters present, raising concerns over ballot integrity.
Observers also pointed to a heavy deployment of military and police forces.

While authorities cited the need for peace and order, Katungod Bangsamoro warned that this display of force, coupled with the deployment of armed police officers inside polling centers to replace withdrawn teachers, “likely discouraged voters and compromised their sense of safety.” /das

articles.title: Denmark says Russian warship fired flares at military helicopter
articles.summary: The Danish prime minister has accused Russia of "reckless" behaviour, while the Kremlin is yet to comment.

blocks.text: Denmark has accused a Russian warship of firing two emergency flares at one of its helicopters while it was tracking the vessel in the Baltic Sea.
The Danish government has summoned the Russian ambassador over the incident, which it said happened during a "routine" monitoring operation on Monday.
Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen branded the Russian action "reckless" and said it was designed to "intimidate and divide".
Moscow has not commented on the incident.

It came on the same day Nato forces shot down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security scare on the alliance's eastern flank, where tensions remain high during Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In a statement detailing the incident in the Baltic Sea, the Danish armed forces said: "One of the air force's Fennec helicopters was today fired at with flares during a routine photographic operation of a Russian frigate, which was located in international waters off Gedser."
Of the two flares fired at the helicopter, one passed close to it, the statement added.
The Danish foreign ministry described the incident as "completely unacceptable".
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen accused Russia of "gradually shifting the boundary for what they consider acceptable behaviour", adding: "That is something we cannot accept."
Overnight, Nato fighter pilots shot down a drone that entered Lithuania's airspace.
Authorities said the drone likely entered southern Lithuania, near the second-largest city of Kaunas, from neighbouring Belarus shortly after midnight on Tuesday.
The origins of the drone are yet to be determined, the Lithuanian national crisis management centre said, but the country's president pointed to increased Russian aggression in recent months.

President Gitanas Nausėda wrote on X: "With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine, such readiness is vital for our region. Together with our Nato Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace."
Lithuania shares a large part of its southern and eastern border with Belarus, a key Russian ally.

Poland also announced there had been "aviation operations" in its airspace on Monday night "due to the activity of Russian Federation's jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory".
It said the overnight operations were of a "preventive nature" and aimed at "securing airspace and its protection, especially in areas adjacent to threatened regions".
Nato jets have been scrambled several times to shoot down stray Ukrainian drones that have crossed into Baltic countries Estonia and Latvia this year.
Ukraine has blamed the stray drones on Russian electronic warfare, technology designed to change the flight paths of Ukrainian drones.

articles.title: NATO fighter jet shoots down drone over Lithuania
articles.summary: An Italian NATO fighter jet shot down a drone over Lithuania ‌shortly after midnight on Tuesday morning, the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre said.

image.caption: Debris of what the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre says is a drone shot down by a NATO fighter jet lies on the ground near Pratkunai, Lithuania, on Tuesday in this screengrab from a handout video. (Lithuanian Army/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
An Italian NATO fighter jet shot down a drone over Lithuania ‌shortly after midnight on Tuesday morning, the Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre said.
It was not immediately clear if the drone was fired by Russian or Ukrainian forces

The drone, which was likely to have entered from Belarus, was shot ​down near Pratkunai village in southern ​Lithuania, near Kaunas, the second-largest city, the centre's spokesperson said. Its origin had yet to be ​determined, he said.
Military drones ​straying into the ⁠airspace of Russia's neighbours have stoked concerns that Russia's war in Ukraine is spilling over NATO's borders.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said that strikes close to the alliance's territory would drive the trans-Atlantic organization to increase its support for Kyiv. Rutte also pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance's own defences along its long eastern border with Russia.
Concerns grow over Russia’s incursions into NATO nations

Officials did not say whether ⁠the drone was ⁠believed to be Ukrainian ‌or Russian. In recent months, Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered NATO airspace in the Baltic region. Kyiv says they were steered off course by ⁠Russian signal jamming.
A drone alert was issued earlier in the capital Vilnius and surrounding region.
The Lithuanian army shared video ‌from the site of the crash, showing debris scattered in grass. Some of the parts appeared to be made from wood and some appeared charred.

Fighters ​with the NATO Baltic Air Defence mission have patrolled the skies of ⁠Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia since the Baltic countries joined ⁠the alliance in 2004. The mission's jets shot down stray ⁠Ukrainian ⁠drones over Estonia ​in May, and over Latvia in June and August.
Denmark reports encounter with Russian ship

Separately, Denmark said a Russian frigate fired two flares towards a Danish military helicopter on Monday. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called the incident "unacceptable" and said it could have endangered human lives.

Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the incident was serious but not surprising, calling it part of a ⁠pattern in which an increasingly aggressive Russia has intensified its hybrid warfare against Europe and is testing NATO.
How NATO is tracking airspace threats over eastern Europe
The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Baltic Sea region is on high alert after incidents involving gas pipeline ​outages, airspace violations and drone sightings.
Russia has dismissed accusations over such incidents and repeatedly denied carrying out hybrid attacks in Europe.

In fighting on Tuesday, a Russian drone attack ‌killed one person ​and knocked out ​power in parts ​of the ⁠city ⁠of Zaporizhzhia ‌in southeast Ukraine, the ⁠acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said.

As well, the regional governor of Odesa, Oleh Kiper, said that Russia hit port ‌infrastructure in ​Ukraine's southern ​Black Sea region overnight, ‌with residential buildings, ‌logistics facilities and transport infrastructure ​coming under attack.
‌Russian ​forces hit ​a cargo ship ​and ⁠a ⁠ferry ‌carrying ⁠military supplies ‌in ​Ukraine's ⁠port ⁠of Chornomorsk, ⁠the ⁠Russian Defence ​Ministry ⁠said on ⁠Tuesday.

U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday posted on social media that Russia and Ukraine had agreed "not to hit" each other's energy infrastructure. He had earlier called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying ​the attacks were causing a shortage of the fuel that is "hurting ​the world."
Trump didn't offer further details on the purported agreement.
Zelenskyy said late Monday that Kyiv was "ready to support de-escalation," but expressed doubts Russia would adhere to such a demand.

articles.title: Court urges public to send questions for amici curiae
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday encouraged the public to submit questions for the retired Supreme Court justices who will appear as amici curiae (friends of the court) to help resolve…

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 15, 2026 6:06pm

The Senate impeachment court on Tuesday encouraged the public to submit questions for the retired Supreme Court justices who will appear as amici curiae (friends of the court) to help resolve questions on the voting threshold for convicting Vice President Sara Duterte.
In a press conference, court spokesperson lawyer Regie Tongol said the public may submit questions through the Senate of the Philippines’ official Facebook page.

“We are expecting those posts on our Senate Facebook page. So, I need to coordinate with the Secretariat regarding the questions submitted there. And perhaps by tonight, we will collate those questions,” Tongol said.
He, however, said the court would select questions that are new and may not be raised by the senator-judges.
“Of course, if those questions have already been asked, we won’t have the presiding officer ask them again since they will already have been answered,” he explained.
Tongol said the court would screen the questions to ensure they are novel and unlikely to be raised by the senator-judges.
"We will only submit questions that are sufficiently complex and necessary to the presiding officer,” he said.

Tongol previously announced that the following legal luminaries will physically appear before the impeachment court on Wednesday, September 16, to present their expert opinions on the ruling regarding the 16-vote threshold for convicting Duterte:

items: Retired Supreme Court Chief Justice Artemio Panganiban — served as the 21st Chief Justice of the Supreme Court from December 2005 to December 2006;
Retired Supreme Court Chief Justice Reynato Puno — served as Chief Justice from December 2006 to May 2010, after serving as an Associate Justice from 1993 to 2006; and

Retired Supreme Court Associate Justice Adolf Azcuna — served as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court and is also a framer of the 1987 Constitution. The Supreme Court has specifically described him as the principal author of Article XI, which deals with accountability of public officers, including impeachment.

blocks.text: Retired Supreme Court Chief Justice Hilario Davide Jr. will also participate, but through a legal memorandum instead of a physical appearance.

Tongol said the amici curiae are expected to answer questions on whether the phrase “all the Members of the Senate,” as stated in Article XI, Section 3, Paragraph 6 of the Constitution, should refer to the Senate’s full membership of 24 senators or only those “who are legally and physically capacitated to participate and vote on the final question in an impeachment trial.”

The amici curiae are also set to face questions related to the Avelino v. Cuenco case, particularly whether its treatment of members beyond the Senate’s coercive jurisdiction applies to senators who are detained, abroad, suspended or whose whereabouts are unknown.
The questions will seek to determine whether such senators should be included in the phrase “all the Members of the Senate” for purposes of the two-thirds vote required under the Constitution.

They are also expected to give their views on whether a senator-judge who did not attend or substantially participate in the impeachment proceedings, including in propounding questions to and observing the demeanor of witnesses, may nevertheless validly cast a vote on the final question in an impeachment trial.
The oral arguments between the defense and prosecution panels on the matter will be held a week later, on September 23, with each side given 15 minutes to present its position, according to Tongol..
After the oral arguments, the senator-judges are also expected to cast their votes on the matter on the same day.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Democrats say supreme court rejection of Trump mail ballot restrictions will ensure ‘safe, secure and accurate elections’ – US politics live
articles.summary: Comments come after court on Monday rejected the president’s mail ballot restrictions ahead of the November midterm elections

blocks.text: Key events

items: 10m agoTrump facing AI backlash in Congress as push for guardrails intensifies
28m agoSupreme court rejection of Trump mail ballot restrictions will ensure 'safe, secure and accurate elections'

blocks.text: Trump facing AI backlash in Congress as push for guardrails intensifies

blocks.caption: David Smith

blocks.text: David Smith
Donald Trump is facing a rare backlash from the US Congress as Democrats and some Republicans push for guardrails on the world’s most powerful AI companies.
Concerns over the dangerous potential of AI reached fever pitch this week after tech leaders sounded the alarm over the rapid advancement of the technology and its potential threat to humanity.

Trump dismissed the anxieties on Monday, describing them as a “HOAX” and “conspiracy” and insisting on social media: “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

But the 80-year-old president, who has sidelined Congress on numerous issues during his second term, looks increasingly isolated as members of both major parties acknowledged the risks and expressed a desire to act before it was too late.

Don Beyer, a Democratic congressman from Virginia, said: “History will look very poorly on that tweet. He’s not paying attention – or he’s paying attention to the wrong people. He’s being really foolish: not the first time he’s been really foolish but perhaps catastrophically foolish in this case.”

Recent surveys by the University of Maryland’s Program for Public Consultation found 85% of Democrats and 79% of Republicans want a new federal agency to monitor and regulate AI; and 82% of Democrats and 78% of Republicans favour government safety tests for AI making critical decisions.
Supreme court rejection of Trump mail ballot restrictions will ensure 'safe, secure and accurate elections'
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Lawmakers have given their support to the supreme court’s rejection of Donald Trump’s bid to restrict mail ballots for the midterm elections.
The decision capped a flurry of last-minute legal action with voting already underway, with states allowed to continue sending out mail ballots under the same processes used for years.

Election officials have said there was simply no way to carry out a complete overhaul in the weeks before the midterms. Alabama, North Carolina and Wisconsin began sending mail ballots to voters over the past week while the new system was still not active.

Washington’s secretary of state Steve Hobbs, a Democrat, said the decision means work “to carry out a safe, secure, and accurate election” can continue ‘without having to upend our election processes to meet unrealistic ballot mail requirements.”

In Arizona, another largely vote-by-mail state, Democratic secretary of state Adrian Fontes said “it is crucial for us to continue rejecting the notion that access and security are mutually exclusive when it comes to running strong elections.”

Utah Lt Gov Deidre Henderson, a Republican serving as the state’s chief election officer, said on social media that the supreme court’s decision means “Utahns can have confidence that the 2026 election will proceed as normal.”
In other developments:

items: Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old former Senate majority leader from Kentucky, was seen in Washington for the first time in months on Monday, minutes before his office released a statement saying that he was back at work.

With a slip of the tongue reminiscent of Joe Biden, Gavin Newsom, California’s Democratic governor, told CNN that he would not run for president in 2028 if his fellow Californian, former vice-president Kamala Harris, decides to run again, since “I know what that means: I know her base of supporters, I know her friends, the zen diagram on that is just pure crossover.”
Donald Trump claimed there is a “SICK conspiracy” against artificial intelligence and data centers in response to the growing calls for greater checks on AI development.

In a statement posted on social media, Barack Obama, the former US president, called for the pace of AI development to be slowed to allow time for the federal government to develop regulations to address “serious safety concerns”.

articles.title: Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter
articles.summary: Denmark has summoned Russia's ambassador over a Baltic Sea encounter that Copenhagen says is part of an increasingly aggressive pattern of Russian behavior.

image.caption: Denmark's military uses the related Fennec helicopter for tasks including surveillance and reconnaissanceImage: gemeinfrei

blocks.text: A Russian warship fired two flares toward a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea, with one passing close to the aircraft, Denmark's armed forces said on Tuesday.
The confrontation comes amid heightened security concerns on NATO's eastern flank during Russia's war in Ukraine.
How has Denmark responded?
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the incident fitted a broader pattern of increasingly aggressive Russian behavior in Europe.
She accused Moscow of intensifying its "hybrid war against Europe" and testing and challenging NATO, and called on European countries to strengthen their defenses.

"Reckless action from Russia towards Danish military during a routine overflight yesterday. Russian actions are meant to intimidate and divide. They will not succeed. We will not waver," Frederiksen said in a statement on X.
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen condemned the incident as "completely unacceptable" and summoned Russia's ambassador, saying the action could have put lives at risk.
The foreign minister accused Moscow of "gradually shifting the boundary for what they consider acceptable behaviour," adding: "That is something we cannot accept."
What happened in the Baltic Sea?
Denmark's armed forces said one of its Fennec helicopters was carrying out a routine photographic reconnaissance mission when the incident occurred.
The helicopter was observing a Russian frigate in international waters off Gedser, a Danish port on the Baltic Sea.
The Russian vessel fired two flares towards the helicopter, according to the Danish military.
"One of the flares passed at close range to the helicopter," it said. No one on board was injured.

The incident came against a backdrop of growing tensions along NATO's eastern flank. Poland has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets during Russian attacks on neighboring Ukraine and reported incursions by Russian drones into its airspace.

NATO members in the region have stepped up air patrols and other defenses as Moscow's war in Ukraine has increasingly raised fears of spillover and direct confrontations between Russian and alliance forces.

articles.title: Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
articles.summary: Following Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla's announcement that Harry Roque's asylum bid in Europe has been denied, Malacañang said the former spokesperson's political persecution claims were…

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 6:00pm
Former presidential spokesperson and congressman Harry Roque Jr. answers questions at the House of Representatives Quad Committee hearing on Aug. 23, 2024.
HREP

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said on Tuesday, September 15, that the asylum request and political persecution claims of former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque lacked basis as he continues to face charges in the Philippines.
According to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, during a press briefing, aside from qualified human trafficking complaints, Roque also faces accusations of land grabbing and tax evasion.

“Ang paniniwala ng PCO (Presidential Communications Office) ay wala pong batayan ang ginawang request ni Harry Roque na sinasabing political persecution lang ang ginagawa sa kanya. Maliwanag naman po ang mga kaso, hindi lang qualified human trafficking,” Castro said.
(The PCO believes that Harry Roque’s request claiming he’s experiencing political persecution has no basis. The cases are clear, and they involve not only qualified human trafficking.)
The Palace’s comment came after Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a separate press briefing earlier Tuesday that Roque’s asylum request had been denied.
Remulla previously said Roque was applying for asylum in Austria, citing political persecution.

In the Philippines, Roque faces non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges filed by the Department of Justice over his alleged active participation in the operations of Lucky South 99, the illegal Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) hub in Pampanga, which was raided in 2024.
An arrest warrant was issued by a Pampanga court against Roque and his co-accused in May 2025 for the qualified human trafficking case.

Meanwhile, in March this year, a group of farmers from Bataan filed land-grabbing complaints against Roque for allegedly transferring land titles, which were supposed to be distributed to 100 farmers, to a private corporation connected to a POGO firm.
The corporation's listed address supposedly pointed to Roque’s office.

The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) also filed a tax evasion case against Roque and his wife in April this year for allegedly failing to pay P3.35 million in taxes connected to transactions involving Biancham Holdings and Trading Inc.
Roque denied all accusations, saying these are all part of the continuous political attacks against him.
He also dismissed Remulla’s claim that his asylum request had been denied, calling it “fake news.”
Roque, who served as the Palace spokesperson under then-President Rodrigo Duterte, left the Philippines in 2024.

articles.title: IBP: No BARMM election-related complaints received
articles.summary: MANTICAO, Misamis Oriental — The Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) did not receive a single formal election-related complaint while its monitors conducted roving operations in various polling…

blocks.text: MANTICAO, Misamis Oriental — The Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) did not receive a single formal election-related complaint while its monitors conducted roving operations in various polling centers during Monday’s historic Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections.
Atty. Allan Panolong, IBP president, said they were prepared to provide legal assistance related to the elections but no voter had sought their assistance.
He noted the IBP monitors had spoken with voters who had finished casting their ballots as well as those waiting to vote.
“We were very much ready to assist complainants on that day, but we didn’t encounter any,” he told the Inquirer.
Panolong acknowledged that some voters may have been hesitant to report their concerns out of fear or they just want no trouble.
He described the overall conduct of the elections in the BARMM as “generally peaceful, orderly and successful.”

While there were election fraud cases such as pre-shading of ballots in Maluso, Basilan, Panolong lauded the Commission on Elections (Comelec) for promptly addressing the matter by suspending polling in the affected precincts.

Panolong played down the violent election-related incidents, particularly in Cotabato City where at least four people were killed and about two dozen others were wounded, saying they did not disrupt the overall voting process.
He commended the military and police for maintaining peace and order around polling centers, noting they were able to contain unruly crowds from entering voting centers.
While the heavy security presence was criticized by some as security “overkill,” Panolong said the deployment was necessary to protect voters and maintain peace and order.
Panolong urged the winners of the BARMM parliamentary elections to work toward improving the welfare and living conditions of Bangsamoro communities.
“We expect them to work hard and move forward for the welfare of the Bangsamoro,” he said.
Panolong said one of the first priorities of the newly elected members of parliament should be the organization of its leadership, including the election of the chief minister and speaker.
According to him, the successful conduct of the elections marked an important moment for the Bangsamoro.
“We are happy that we were part of this historic event,” Panolong said. /gsg

These six representatives come from the settler communities, women, youth, traditional leaders, and Ulama (Muslim religious leaders) sectors. Elected bets will join the Bangsamoro Parliament alongside the two Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples (NMIP) representatives selected earlier in August.
As of 4:59 pm on Tuesday, September 15, 98.64% of total election returns show that the leading sectoral representatives are:

items: Yul Adelfo Olaya as a representative for settler communities – 747,214 votes

blocks.text: These six leading candidates for sectoral representatives were chosen through the direct plurality of valid votes cast for nominees in their representative sectors. In contrast, the NMIP representatives were chosen during a regional inter-tribal convention based on customary law. In every election cycle, the chosen representatives will rotate among the region’s six major non-Moro indigenous groups: the Teduray, Lambangian, Erumanen ne Menuvu, Dulangan Manobo, Blaan, and Limbubungan Higaonon.

articles.title: Pensioners are ‘big winners’ with triple-lock set to rise by 3.9%, lifting state pension to £13,000 – business live
articles.summary: Wage growth – used to set triple-lock pension – slows to 3.9%, meaning state pension should hit £13,000 next year

blocks.text: State pension set to rise by 3.9% after wage growth data
The UK state pension is set to rise by 3.9% next year, it appears, following today’s wage growth figures.
Under the triple-lock system, pensions rise by the highest of average earnings, inflation, or 2.5%.

So today’s data showing that total pay rose by 3.9% over the last year is likely to be the figure used to set the pension increase (unless we get a surge of inflation in September’s data to 4% or higher).
Assuming, of course, that the government continue to stick with the triple-lock – as there are calls to suspend it.
Jon Greer, head of retirement policy at Quilter, says:

double quotation mark“Today’s earnings figures show wage growth running at 3.9%, which puts a State Pension increase of a similar magnitude firmly on the cards next April under the triple lock. “If confirmed, this would see the full New State Pension rise to over £13,000. While we will need to wait for September’s inflation figure before the uprating mechanism is formally confirmed, inflation is currently expected to remain below earnings growth, making an earnings-led increase the most likely outcome. “For pensioners, another above-inflation increase will be welcome news and reflects the success of the triple lock in strengthening the value of the State Pension over time. The State Pension remains a crucial source of retirement income for millions of people and continues to provide the foundation upon which many build the rest of their retirement plans.
Key events

items: 3m agoRBC BlueBay: this is a very weak employment report beneath the surface
32m agoSchool uniform spending drops in cost of living squeeze

2h agoHow some pensioners could still avoid tax

3h agoHargreaves Lansdown: Pensioners to get £490 boost under triple lock
4h agoState pension set to rise by 3.9% after wage growth data
4h agoVacancies dip again.
4h agoIntroduction: UK jobs market under the spotlight

blocks.text: RBC BlueBay: this is a very weak employment report beneath the surface
Today’s UK jobs report is “very weak” beneath the surface, warns Mike Bell, head of market strategy for RBC BlueBay.

double quotation markToday’s UK jobs data is much weaker below the surface than the headline number suggests. The headline data is being hugely flattered by a surge in admin and support service and education jobs. The vast majority of private sectors are shedding jobs. The cumulative decline in employment from the peak in some sectors is becoming quite alarming.

blocks.caption: Photograph: RBC BlueBay

blocks.text: Bell adds:

double quotation markAlso of concern is that employment in professional services and construction is now starting to decline along with the longstanding weakness in sectors like retail, hospitality, manufacturing and tech. The decline in employment is broad based across regions too.
The government’s policy that pensioners whose only income is the state pension won’t pay tax creates “an unusual divide”, says Ian Futcher, financial planner at Quilter:
With the state pension set to rise over the tax-free personal allowance next year, Futcher says:

double quotation markSomeone relying solely on the State Pension will be protected from paying tax, while a pensioner who has built up even a relatively modest private pension could still find themselves facing a tax bill. After spending decades encouraging people to save for retirement, the system risks creating a cliff edge where those who have made additional provision can be treated less favourably than those relying entirely on the State Pension.
School uniform spending drops in cost of living squeeze

blocks.caption: Julia Kollewe

blocks.text: Julia Kollewe

Parents and carers in Great Britain spent 12.5% less on school uniform in the run-up to the start of this academic year, turning to promotions and second-hand items to keep expenses down as families struggled with the cost of living crisis.

The average spend on school uniform was £54.53 in the four weeks to 6 September, down an eighth from £62.29 in the same period last year, according to the market research company Worldpanel by Numerator. Overall grocery inflation picked up to 2.3% from 2.1%.

The monthly report also showed that branded goods outpaced supermarkets’ cheaper own-label items for only the second time in the past year, with sales up 3.7% compared to 2.9% growth for own label – a reversal of a pattern that has defined much of this year. Despite this shift, shoppers have kept a strong appetite for promotions. Spending on grocery deals rose by £243m, or 7% year on year, significantly outstripping full-price sales growth of just 1.4%.
Grocery-only sales at Marks & Spencer jumped 14.8% year on year, measured by till spend, i.e. the value of sales (so also reflecting price rises).

Sales at Asda rose by 0.1% over the 12 weeks to 6 September, as the grocer returned to growth for the first time since March 2024. However, the Leeds-based retailer’s market share dipped to 11.5%, with a higher share of 16% in the north of England. It outperformed the market in areas such as hot drinks, ice cream and chilled poultry.

The online grocersupermarket Ocado, with sales up by 13.3%, remained the fastest -growing grocer overall, used by 4.4% of households, with a slightly higher market share of 2.2%. Lidl moved up to 8.7% of the market, from 8.3% a year ago. Sales rose by 8%, lifted by strong performance across confectionery, soft drinks and fresh produce.

Sales at Sainsbury’s were 2.9% higher than last year. The UK’s second largest grocer was just ahead of and Morrisons, where till spend rose by 2.8%, and the two supermarket chains maintained their previous market share of 15.2% and 8.4%, respectively.

At Tesco, the UK’s largest supermarket, sales rose by 1.7%, but its market share dipped to 27.8% from 28.1%. The German discounter Aldi’s sales edged 0.7% higher, giving it a slightly lower market of 10.6% share.
Sales at the Co-op were up by 2.9%, with market share flat at 5.5%. Waitrose sales grew by 2.8%, with its market share also stable, at 4.5%.
European markets in the red as US Treasury 10-year yield rises over 5%
European stock markets are in the red this morning, as investors fret about the ongoing sell-off in the bond market and the rising oil price (the two are linked!).
Britain’s FTSE 100 share index has lost 90 points, or 0.85%, to 10,606 points this morning.
Germany’s DAX and France’s CAC 40 are both down around 0.7%.
Neil Wilson, investor strategist at Saxo UK, says “Financials and miners are bearing the brunt in Europe, while AI stocks are down across Asia and the US.”
Investors seem rattled that the US 10-year Treasury yield has risen over 5% this week.
Wilson adds:

double quotation markThe US Treasury 10-year yield broke 5% for the first time since 2023 on Monday and advanced to a 19-year high as it touched 5.03% this morning...is this the point at which markets break? 5.25% is really when it gets dicey. Markets are pricing in a 93% chance the Fed hikes rates this week. While there are lots of reasons behind the bond rout, BMO says Treasury yields and oil prices haven’t been this closely correlated for seven years.
Today’s jobs report also shows that the retail and hospitality sector continued to lose jobs over the summer.
The British Retail Consortium has calculated that there are 122,000 fewer jobs in retail than two years ago, which will limit job opportunities for young people.
Stephen Evans, chief executive at Learning and Work Institute (L&W), explains:

double quotation mark“Headline stability in the job stats masks two underlying and related challenges. The first is that one million young people are not in education, employment or training, risking long-term harm to their career prospects. Ramping up efforts to change that can’t wait. The second is the stalling of job growth in parts of the private sectors like retail and hospitality, down 150,000 payroll jobs since last year. This limits first job opportunities for young people and reflects underlying economic weakness that ongoing international uncertainty won’t help. The employment rate is relatively high by international standards, but risks trending in the wrong direction with 3.9 million people not in work but saying they want a job.”
The drop in company vacancies over the last few months suggests demand for workers is weakening, warns Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales:

double quotation mark“The ongoing drop in vacancies should set alarm bells ringing for the jobs market, as it suggests that demand for workers is wilting under the weight of soaring staffing costs, onerous regulation and increased automation. “The UK labour market could be heading for a rockier autumn, as rising energy bills and pre-Budget tax uncertainty increasingly curb hiring intentions, resulting in moderately higher unemployment and lower pay growth.
The debate over the triple lock is set to be reignited by today’s news that the state pensions could rises by 3.9% next year.
So predicts Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club:

double quotation markPay growth is cooling, with regular earnings growth (including bonuses) easing to 3.9%, but that is hardly enough to make the inflation problem disappear. This snapshot points to a 3.9% rise in the state pension next April under the triple lock, with average earnings growth, the measure used for the calculation, being pushed higher by particularly strong public sector pay growth. Public sector pay is running at 6.3%, more than twice the 2.9% pace in the private sector, which reflects the impact of pay awards and the timing of them. That’s likely to reignite the debate around the triple lock, particularly when government debt is already so high, and the cost of servicing it is painfully expensive. It may be even more controversial given that a pay measure which has been boosted by public sector wage awards is helping drive up the state pension bill at the same time as the government is already under pressure to contain spending and borrowing.
US government borrowing costs hit 19-year high
The bond market sell-off is continuing this morning, although the UK is avoiding the worst of it.
US government bonds, or Treasuries, are weakening, which is driving up the yield (or interest rate) on 10-year bonds back over 5% to the highest level since 2007.
UK bond yields are only slightly higher. They might be being suppressed by reports that the Bank of England will halt its sale of long-dated government bonds later this week.
That “quantitative tightening” programme has been blamed for boosting supplies of bonds in the market, pushing up yields.
How some pensioners could still avoid tax
If the state pension rises to £13,000 next year, it will probably breach the UK’s tax-free personal allowance (currently £12,570) – the amount you can earn before paying income tax.
However, pensioners who don’t receive any other income should still be exempt from paying tax if the state pension exceeds the personal allowance.
The House of Commons Library explains:

double quotation markIn the 2025 Budget the government announced the personal allowance would be frozen at its current level up to April 2031. It also announced that pensioners whose sole income is the basic or new state pension would not have to pay small amounts of tax via simple assessment from 2027/28 if the new or basic state pension exceeded the personal allowance from that point. To date the government has not published any further details of how this is to be done.
However, if you had a private pension too, or earnings from dividends or bank interest, then you would be taxed on the earnings over the personal allowance.
Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, has spotted that private sector employment has dropped since the start of the year.
He says:

double quotation mark“The latest UK jobs numbers suggest the labour market remains subdued. Unemployment was little changed over the summer, but payroll employment and vacancies continued to drop. “Payroll employment fell 26,000 in August, while July’s 13,000 fall was revised bigger. The public sector continued to flatter the numbers. Private-sector employment fell, leaving it almost 141,000 lower than at the start of the year, but the public sector headcount continued to rise, up almost 36,000 since January.
Resolution: Pensioners are big winners today, private sector workers are the losers
The Resolution Foundation have spotted that private sector pay growth in the UK has fallen to its weakest level since the start of the decade.
At just 2.9% per year in May-July, pay growth in the private sector is the joint lowest rate since October 2020.
That’s weaker than the overall total pay growth of 3.9%, which is likely to be used to set the triple lock next year (see earlier post).

blocks.caption: Photograph: ONS

blocks.text: Worryingly, Resolution Foundation also forecasts that wages are “set to shrink significantly in the second half of the year as inflation rises”.
Julia Diniz, economist at the Resolution Foundation, said:

double quotation mark“The big winners from today’s ONS data are pensioners, who are set for another large rise in the state pension next spring thanks to the triple lock. “The biggest losers are workers in the private sector who are already earning less than they were last autumn. With wage growth slumping to its lowest rate in nearly six years, the UK’s private sector pay squeeze will tighten over the coming months as inflation rises. “With unemployment settling at around five per cent and the number of job vacancies continuing to fall, conditions are also tough for those looking for work, especially young people.”
The slowdown in total pay growth over the summer, and the drop in payrolled employeers, may deter the Bank of England from raising interest rates at its next meeting later this week.
The money markets indicate there’s a 67% chance that the Bank holds interest rates on Thursday.
Sanjay Raja, chief UK economist at Deutsche Bank, says the labour market still looks “sluggish”:

double quotation markWhile economic growth continues to outpace expectations, the staggering fact is that it’s happening with fewer employees. Productivity growth, by definition, is pushing higher. That said, there’s no evidence yet that the UK labour market is out of the woods just yet. For the MPC, this will matter. A still sluggish labour market will give the Bank some confidence that Bank Rate remains restrictive.
Supporters of the pension triple lock point out that it has lifted the living standards of the UK’s poorest pensioners.
Critics, though, argue that it has been more expensive than expected, and ties the government into increasing the pension bill each year regardless of economic conditions.
The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) have worked out that by 2050, the triple lock could have cost as much as £40bn, although the calculations are rather murky.
They say:

items: The triple lock has increased annual spending on the state pension by around £16 billion, compared with uprating in line with average earnings growth since 2010.

Current forecasts from the Office for Budget Responsibility suggest that the triple lock will push up state pension spending by £600 million per year in 2029–30, compared with a baseline of increases in line with average earnings.

While this is small compared with total state pension spending (of £154 billion per year), each increase adds up over time and the triple lock’s ratcheting effect permanently locks in increases in spending. This is both costly and very uncertain in the long run, because it depends on the exact path of inflation and earnings.

We estimate that by 2050 keeping the triple lock would, in expectation, cost around £20 billion per year in today’s terms. But the high uncertainty means that, in fact, the cost could reasonably be anywhere between £5 billion and £40 billion per year.

blocks.text: Hargreaves Lansdown: Pensioners to get £490 boost under triple lock
Helen Morrissey, head of retirement analysis at Hargreaves Lansdown, is also expecting the state pension to rise by 3.9% next year under the triple-lock system.
Morrissey explains:

double quotation mark“Pensioners stand to be almost £490 better off next year as today’s earnings figures have a huge impact on next year’s state pension. The data, alongside September’s inflation figure and 2.5%, is a key component of the triple lock formula used to increase state pensions. With CPI inflation currently sitting at 2.9% it seems increasingly likely that today’s 3.9% increase in average earnings will be the figure used. This would put someone on the full new state pension on course to receive £250.70 per week from next April – up from the current £241.30 per week. Someone on a full basic state pension would receive £192.10 per week – up from £184.90.
Vacancies dip again.
The estimated number of vacancies in the UK decreased in the latest quarter.
The ONS esimates that in June to August there was a decrease of 8,000 (1.1%) to 702,000, compared with March to May 2026.
ONS director of economic statistics Liz McKeown says:

double quotation mark“Vacancies remain at their lowest level outside the pandemic period for more than a decade, with smaller businesses continuing to report that increased labour costs are affecting hiring decisions.”
The Office for National Statistics has also found that the number of ‘workforce jobs’ in the UK has dropped.
It says:

double quotation markThe estimated number of workforce jobs in the UK was 36.7 million in June 2026. This is a decrease of 48,000 (0.1%) from March 2026, with decreases of 43,000 (1.0%) in the self-employment jobs component and a decrease of 10,000 (0.0%) in the employee jobs component.
Introduction: UK jobs market under the spotlight
Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.
UK companies continued to shed jobs over the summer, as wage growth slowed, new data shows.
The latest labour market report, just released, shows that the number of employees on company payrolls fell by 26,000 in August, and dropped by 145,000 compared with August 2025.
Despite that drop, though, the UK’s unemployment rate for people aged 16 years and over remains at 4.9% for the May to July quarter.
Workers’ pay packets are being squeezed, though, especially in the private sector.
Total pay growth (including bonuses) slowed to 3.9% in May to July, down from 4.2% on the previous three-month period. Regular pay (excluding bonuses) growth stuck at 3.5%.
But while private sector pay rose by 2.9%, annual average regular earnings growth was 6.3% for the public sector. That’s because NHS staff pay rises were paid out earlier this year.

double quotation mark“The labour market remains broadly stable, with employment and unemployment rates largely unchanged in the latest period. However, payrolled employee numbers continue to edge down, with falls over the past year particularly evident in the retail and hospitality sectors. “Regular wage growth has remained relatively stable in recent months, while total pay growth, which includes bonuses, has eased and was last lower nearly six years ago. There remains a notable difference between public and private sector pay growth, with public sector figures continuing to be affected by the timing of NHS pay awards this year.”
The agenda

items: 7am BST: UK labour market report
8am BST: UK grocery inflation report
10am BST: Eurozone industrial production report for July
1.30pm BST: US retail sales report

articles.title: Former Comelec chief wins Cotabato City 1st district representative race
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairperson Sheriff Abas has won the representative race in the first district of Cotabato City for the first Bangsamoro Parliamentary…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairperson Sheriff Abas has won the representative race in the first district of Cotabato City for the first Bangsamoro Parliamentary elections with over 12,000 votes.

According to the data server of election watchdog Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting as of 3:51 p.m. on Tuesday, Abas obtained 12,334 votes. This is 57.8 percent of the total 21,356 votes cast in the district.
Abas ran under United Bangsamoro Justice Party, the political party of Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
Abas’ rivals Romeo Sema and Danilo Liggayo obtained 8,676 votes and 346 votes, respectively.
In a Facebook post past midnight Monday, Abas thanked the constituent who supported and voted for him.

Meanwhile, Abas was the subject of a show cause order (SCO) issued by the Comelec over the weekend due to allegations of vote-buying ahead of the parliamentary elections. He was asked to explain why a complaint or election offense or petition for disqualification should not be filed against him.
In issuing the SCO, Comelec’s Committee on Kontra Bigay cited a Facebook post showing a photo of a sample ballot with “VOTE #3 SA BALOTA ATTY. SHERIFF ABAS” along with three P1,000 bills.
In a separate Facebook post last Saturday, Abas called on the public to verify information and to avoid spreading false information.
“Walang lugar ang fake news at paninira sa halalan. Kung may alegasyon, idaan sa tamang proseso at sa COMELEC, hindi sa social media,” he wrote.
(Fake news has no place in elections. If there are allegations, course it through proper process and Comelec, and not in social media.)
Abas was Comelec chairperson from 2017 to 2022. He was the first Comelec chief from Mindanao. /mr

articles.title: Serving healthy food now mandatory in Baguio City's public events
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — Serving healthy food at city government events and meetings will be mandatory starting Sept. 19 following the publication of an ordinance creating a healthier food environment in the…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — Serving healthy food at city government events and meetings will be mandatory starting Sept. 19 following the publication of an ordinance creating a healthier food environment in the city. “With the ordinance, no public funds should be spent on unhealthy food. articles.summary: Following his confinement in the Quezon City Jail due to allegations of plunder, the Palace said no special treatment would be allowed of former House speaker Martin Romualdez.

blocks.text: Published September 15, 2026 5:44pm
Following his confinement in the Quezon City Jail due to allegations of plunder, the Palace said no special treatment would be allowed to former House speaker Martin Romualdez.

A cousin of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., Romualdez was indicted with plunder after being accused of receiving around P7.44 billion in kickbacks from bogus flood control and infrastructure projects.
After a lengthy petition for a hospital stay, Romualdez is now in an infirmary ward in the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory.

“Kung ano po ang sinasapit ngayon ng mga ‘di umanong sangkot, iyan naman po ay walang dapat sinisinong. Mayaman, mahirap, ordinaryong tao, may kapangyarihan. Kung nakagawa man ng mali sa taumbayan, kailangan lang din pong pantay-pantay kung ano po ang naranasan ng mga akusado. So wala pong dapat na special treatment,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a press briefing on Tuesday.

(Whatever the accused is facing right now, it really should not be selective. Rich, poor, ordinary people, the powerful. If a wrong was committed against the public, the accused should experience equal treatment. So there should be no special treatment.)
However, Castro maintained that as long as the court has not issued a conviction, all suspects under the law are innocent until proven otherwise.

Asked why Marcos’ planned visit to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Monday was cancelled, Castro said it was likely due to his schedule. She added the President had just arrived from his visit in India on the same day and had another engagement.
Romualdez had been confined in the PGH after the Sandiganbayan Third Division ordered an independent assessment of whether or not he needed to stay confined in the hospital.
After PGH doctors said that the Leyte representative was fit to be detained, Romualdez was transferred to the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory on Monday night. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: One of Sydney’s largest councils joins ban on ‘pervert’ glasses at local swimming pools
articles.summary:
Councillors say locals have been raising concerns about people secretly filming in change rooms, swimming pools and around schools

  • Get our

blocks.text: One of Sydney’s largest councils has joined the City of Brisbane and the City of Yarra to issue a ban on AI smart glasses at public pools as concerns mount over the potential for predators to exploit the new technology.
On Tuesday evening, Canterbury-Bankstown voted overwhelmingly in favour of banning the tech at its local pools, with its mayor, Bilal El-Hayek, describing them as “pervert glasses”.
Since their release, there have been reports of women being filmed without their consent and their interactions with a glasses-wearing influencer posted on social media.

“Chat groups, Facebook, local community forums and Tik Tok are just some of the online platforms where women are venting their concerns over the smart technology that threatens both safety and privacy,” El-Hayek told councillors at the meeting.
“Their biggest concerns are around ‘perverts and paedophiles’ secretly filming in change rooms, swimming pools and around schools.

“The latest AI smart glasses are wearable devices with high resolution cameras … and AI powered features like real time translation, object recognition and open-ear audio … these glasses can not only film, record and share footage, they can also scan your face and potentially access and retrieve information about you.”
Last month, Brisbane became the first council in Australia to publicly announce a ban on covert filming at its 21 public pools amid growing fears to protect child safety.

The head of policy at Digital Rights Watch, Tom Sulston, praised the decision. He said it was “vital that councils across Australia ensure that public spaces like swimming pools are safe for families to enjoy without the threat of unwanted video surveillance”.

“We all need to be able to go out in public without fear of being covertly recorded and having the images uploaded to the internet without our consent,” he said. “We look forward to seeing not just councils following Brisbane’s lead, but also state and federal governments.”

Yarra in inner Melbourne followed suit, voting last week to ban smart glasses from its leisure and aquatic facilities, childcare centres and playgrounds. It also confirmed it would call on the federal government to bring in stronger privacy laws to protect people from new technologies.

Randwick council in Sydney’s eastern suburbs has also banned the new technology at the Des Renford leisure centre. In a statement to Guardian Australia, it said “growing community concerns” about their potential misuse were behind the decision.

“Signage has been installed at the entrance and anyone wearing smart glasses in the centre will be asked to remove them or leave,” it said. “This precautionary measure will help ensure the centre remains a safe, welcoming and family-friendly place for all visitors.”
The bans will not apply to people with accessibility concerns, including vision impairment.
The federal attorney general, Michelle Rowland, has not ruled out banning the glasses but has indicated how complex the laws are governing the new technology.
In August, she wrote to the privacy commissioner, Carly Kind, raising concerns she’d received from the community about their growing uptake and requesting it be given priority consideration.
“Privacy is an essential part of all our lives; it allows us to be who we are with dignity and without fear,” she said at the time.
“Unlike other forms of technology, smart glasses may be used more discreetly, making it harder to know when you are being recorded.
“The government is continuing to work on the next phase of privacy reforms to ensure our privacy laws are fit for purpose in the digital age.”
Australia’s online safety regulator has urged smartglasses companies to automatically blur people’s faces filmed on the devices, and make it clearer when someone is filming.

In advice to industry published at the end of August, the office of the eSafety commissioner warned that while smartglasses with cameras, such as Meta’s Ray-Ban, can offer accessibility benefits to low vision or blind people, companies might pit “accessibility benefits against safety and privacy considerations”, and noted there was already a backlash to the technology.

articles.title: DOJ summons Robin Padilla, 6 others over Bato Dela Rosa escape
articles.summary: The Department of Justice has issued a subpoena against Sen. Robin Padilla and six others over complaints of obstruction of justice.

blocks.text: September 15, 2026 | 5:31pm

Sen. Robin Padilla voices out his frustration during the first regular Senate session on Sept. 15, 2025 over circulating false reports claiming he made a rude gesture during the national anthem last week.
The Philippine STAR / Jesse Bustos
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Justice (DOJ) has issued a subpoena against Sen. Robin Padilla and six others over complaints of obstruction of justice.
According to the summons, Padilla is required to appear before the DOJ on September 25 and October 9.
The summons were served on the lawmaker and co-accused Lt. Col. Jean Alla Yasin Robles on Tuesday afternoon, according to DOJ Spokesperson Polo Martinez.
The complaints are over his alleged assistance in the escape of Sen. Bato Dela Rosa on May 14, following the shooting incident at the Senate.
It could be recalled that Dela Rosa hitched a ride in Padilla’s SUV on May 14 before disappearing from law enforcement’s radar. Padilla also admitted that he gave Dela Rosa a ride to help him escape.
The DOJ complaint was filed by the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group on May 28.
A separate complaint of obstruction of justice was also filed before the Office of the Ombudsman against Padilla.
The obstruction complaint against Padilla at the Ombudsman was filed by civic group Tindig Pilipinas on July 4.
In a Facebook post, Padilla said: "A subpoena has arrived."
Dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court, is currently at large due to alleged crimes against humanity.

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY – Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua has called for unity among all Bangsamoro leaders and for newly elected officials to accept their mandates with humility and responsibility following the historic Bangsamoro Parliamentary Elections (BPE) on Monday.

“The election is over, but our work does not end here. Now is the time to unite and continue what we have started. Join me in building a stronger Bangsamoro—more peaceful, more just, and more united,” Macacua said Tuesday.
Macacua won as parliamentary representative of Maguindanao del Norte 3rd district over his lone rival, Badrudin Mamad, of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP).
He also prayed for the protection of the Bangsamoro people, especially those physically hurt by the electoral process.

“Protect our people, comfort those affected by violence, guide our leaders, and bless the Bangsamoro with lasting peace, justice, and unity. May You continue to guide us in serving our people and building a better future for everyone,” Macacua, president of Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), said.
He lauded the Bangsamoro people who worked tirelessly for the successful first BPE.

“This historic moment reflects the courage, participation, and hope of every Bangsamoro who cast a vote and believed in a better future,” he said, noting that he felt hurt by the violence that occurred in some areas across the region, particularly in Cotabato City.

“To those who were hurt and those who lost loved ones, we have not forgotten you. Let us not allow violence to divide us. Despite our differences, we share one Bangsamoro and one future. Let us unite, support one another, and choose peace,” he said.
He said the recent political exercises are not only about those who won.

“It is about every Bangsamoro who placed their trust in the process and contributed to shaping our future. To those who have been given a mandate, accept it with humility and full responsibility,” Macacua said./coa

articles.title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption

blocks.text: Parts of the Netherlands, including Amsterdam, have been hit by major rail disruption after suspected sabotage to the tracks, the country's railway operator has said.
ProRail warned that passengers in the country's centre and north should expect cancellations and delays on Tuesday, while several level crossings were also malfunctioning.
Pipes were attached to the tracks in multiple locations, according to local media. In a statement, ProRail said the incident appeared to be "an intentional disruption... caused by human action".
It added that no suspects or motives had been identified, but the national police unit was investigating. The BBC has contacted police for comment.
The network's website showed that 15 disruptions had been recorded across the country on Tuesday, with routes to the main international airport, Schiphol, and Utrecht also affected.
ProRail said in a statement: "Materials were found at multiple locations in the track that were deliberately placed there. This causes section malfunctions. Sabotage appears to be involved".

Footage published by Dutch public broadcaster NOS on Tuesday showed police carrying what appeared to be metal pipes - about 1.5 metres (5ft) - away from railway tracks at Veenendaal in the central Netherlands.

articles.title: PH to host ASEAN Regional Dialogue on Circular Economy on Sept. 22-23
articles.summary: The Philippines will host the ASEAN Regional Dialogue on Circular Economy on September 22 to 23, 2026 as the region shifts away from single-use waste, the Department of Environment and Natural…

blocks.text: Published September 15, 2026 5:02pm

The Philippines will host the ASEAN Regional Dialogue on Circular Economy on September 22 to 23, 2026 as the region shifts away from single-use waste, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said.

The dialogue will explore state-level circular economy strategies, local governance roles, Extended Producer Responsibility regulations, and financial mechanisms that enable businesses and communities to transition.

"Long-term solutions must also address the problem at its source and strengthen measures that can discourage repeated abuse of natural resources," Acting Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna in a statement.
During the two-day regional meet, a session will center on supporting small businesses and informal waste sector workers so they are fully included as regional circular systems expand and formalize.

"For ordinary Filipinos and communities across ASEAN, the Dialogue points to something concrete: cleaner neighborhoods, new livelihoods built around recycling and resource recovery, and stronger safety nets for the informal waste workers who already do much of this work today," the DENR said.

"Because waste and pollution do not stop at borders, the region's response has to be shared, and the Dialogue is designed to turn that shared urgency into partnerships and investments member states can act on."
The event will culminate in an ASEAN Chair's Summary on Circular Economy Policy and Implementation, outlining key policy insights and priority action items, the DENR said.

These recommendations will directly inform the ASEAN Circular Economy Forum in October 2026, advancing regional progress as the Philippines prepares to host the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila this November.
The dialogue will be held at New World Hotel Makati. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Parents seek out school uniform deals, cutting average spend to £54.53
articles.summary: Overall grocery inflation jumps to 2.3%, as Ocado and Lidl gain market share

blocks.text: Parents and carers spent 12.5% less on school uniform in the run-up to the start of this academic year, turning to promotions and second-hand items to keep expenses down as families struggled with the cost of living crisis.

The average spend on school uniform was £54.53 in the four weeks to 6 September, down an eighth from £62.29 in the same period last year, according to the market research company Worldpanel by Numerator. Overall grocery inflation picked up to 2.3% from 2.1%.
Fraser McKevitt, the head of retail and consumer insight at the company, said “value is the watchword for parents this back-to-school season” as they try to balance stretched household budgets.

Almost half of households (44%) prioritised keeping costs low above all else when it comes to buying uniform, even if that means compromising on quality, while a third (33%) aimed to strike a balance between the two, according to a back to school survey conducted by Worldpanel in August.

“It’s a clear sign that, for many families, the return to school is landing at a difficult time financially, and retailers who can offer reassurance on price without compromising on quality stand will stand in good stead,” McKevitt said.

Grocery sales rose 2% year on year over the period, the monthly Worldpanel figures showed. August brought more warm weather and the end of a summer of sport. But with the return to school and work looming for many, shopping habits began to shift. Shoppers made 18m fewer trips to supermarkets compared with a peak of 497m in July.

“The end of the summer holidays typically brings a cooling in trip frequency and a pivot towards priority purchases, and this year is no exception,” McKevitt said. “While grocery inflation ticked up modestly last month, it remains significantly lower than the levels we saw earlier in the year, giving households some welcome breathing room.”

Sandwiches featured in more than half of all kids’ lunchboxes, with more than half a million more households that include children buying loaves of bread in the seven days to 6 September compared with the previous week. The number buying satsumas (+29%) and cucumbers (+21%) also rose in the final week before the return to school.
Sales at Asda rose by 0.1% over the 12 weeks to 6 September, as the grocer returned to growth for the first time since March 2024. However, the Leeds-based retailer’s market share dipped to 11.5%.
after newsletter promotion
The online supermarket Ocado, with sales up by 13.3%, remained the fastest-growing grocer overall, with a slightly higher market share of 2.2%. Lidl moved up to 8.7% of the market.

Sainsbury’s and Morrisons maintained their previous market share of 15.2% and 8.4%, respectively. The UK’s largest supermarket, Tesco, dipped to 27.8% from 28.1%. The German discounter Aldi took a 10.6% share.
